To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high pressure inhibits Na+ and Cl+ pumps, increases passive permeability to Na+ and Cl+, and decreases passive permeability to K+.

1) the Na+ and K+ concentrations in the isolated eel gill increase when the tissue is exposed to pressures of about 1000 atmospheres; 2) the tissue Cl− concentration decreases when the tissue is pressurized; 3) the Na+, K+ ATPase activity is decreased by pressures of about 500 atmospheres and above; 4) the Na+ permeability of the eel gill is increased by pressures of about one thousand atmospheres;
high hydrostatic pressure inhibits the activity (Vmax) of the (Na+,K+)-ATPase and the Na+ and the Cl− pumps in eel gills and that it increases tissue Na+ and Cl- content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of high hydrostatic pressure on the movements of sodium (Na+), potassium (K+) and chlorine (Cl−) in isolated eel (Anguilla anguilla) gills.
the effects of hydrostatic pressure on the transport of Na+, K+, and Cl− in gill tissue from the eel Anguilla anguilla.
the study of the effects of hydrostatic pressure on the ionic movements in eel gills and the mechanisms involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pressure inhibits Na+, K+ ATPase activity and that this effect is the main one in the inhibition of the Na+ and K+ transport.
high hydrostatic pressures induce a decrease in the active transport of Na+, Cl− and K+.
pressure inhibits the Na+ pump and the Cl− pump.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pressure effects are mainly on the passive permeabilities.
the Na+ pump is inhibited by pressure and that this inhibition is the cause of the increase in the tissue content of sodium.
the effects of hydrostatic pressure on Na+, K+ movements in eel gills are similar to those produced by changes in the external Na+ concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high hydrostatic pressure can affect ion transport in isolated gills, and this may have important implications for fish physiology.
the effects of high pressure on the gills can be explained by a combination of effects on both the Na+ and the Cl− pumps and the passive permeabilities.
high hydrostatic pressures can induce changes in the tissue content of Na+, K+, and Cl−, as well as in the activity of the Na+,K+-ATPase in isolated eel (Anguilla rostrata) gills.
